messages:
Maya: FYI a Fortune 100 prospect wants SOC2 in-contract within 10 weeks. Sales asking to commit. Need a quick prioritization call: freeze some features or offer a scoped certification?

Olivia: Customer is firm — legal procurement timeline locks in if we commit. They will push for Dedicated access later, but hosted-first is fine to start. We should weigh near-term ARR vs roadmap velocity.

Lina: Security perspective: propose "SOC2-hosted-only" for first attestation. Exclude Dedicated/private out of scope initially, exclude cross-account integrations. That halves control surface.

Sam: Eng check: core gaps are audit logs with retention, RBAC enforcement across Console/API, SSO/SAML coverage, infra change evidence. Rough estimate: 6-10 engineer-months depending on scope and contractors. With a focused sprint team we could aim ~10 weeks.

Ben: Contracts note: we need milestone language and acceptance criteria. Also confirm if the customer needs SOC2 Type II or Type I. Type I is faster but less valuable as a reference.

Maya: Let's do a quick RICE-ish comparator to decide between SOC2-hosted vs queued Billing Export feature (customer ask).

Maya: RICE sketch for SOC2-hosted: Reach=4 (enterprise deals this quarter), Impact=9 (large ARR + reference), Confidence=0.6, Effort=8 (E-months) => (4*9*0.6)/8 = 2.7

Maya: Billing export (CSV+S3 delivery): Reach=5 (many customers), Impact=5, Confidence=0.8, Effort=3 => (5*5*0.8)/3 = 6.67

Olivia: Billing export actually converts a lot of mid-market accounts. Numbers show it outranks SOC2 in RICE here — but SOC2 has strategic value beyond pure RICE.

Lina: Suggestion: hybrid path — build Billing Export now (lower effort) + offer hosted-only SOC2 carveout with a firm delivery date. Use billing export as short-term unlock for some deals while we run parallel SOC2 readiness sprints for enterprise prospect.

Chris: Operational constraint: if we start SOC2 work, schedule an infra freeze window the week before audit snapshots. Also we'll need a documented rollback & canary policy for any production change during that period.

Sam: Execution plan proposal: Week 0-1 finalize in-scope systems and control binder; Weeks 2-6 implement logs/retention, RBAC, SSO; Weeks 7-8 evidence collection and internal gap run; Week 9 auditor kickoff. Parallelize Billing Export in a separate squad (2 sprints).

Ben: I'll prepare milestone contract language (Type I vs Type II options, hosted-only clause, credits for missed milestones). Also ask the customer if they require ISO; many don't at signing.

Maya: Decision draft: 1) Ship Billing Export within 4 weeks to capture mid-market ARR. 2) Commit to scoped SOC2-hosted Type I + readiness timeline targeting auditor engagement in ~9-10 weeks. 3) Delay Dedicated/private certification until post-Type II roadmap. 4) If timeline slips, offer hosted-only interim agreement with service credits.

Olivia: I'll communicate the hybrid option to the customer and secure a conditional LOI.

Lina: I'll post a minimal controls checklist and the acceptance criteria doc by Monday morning (access control, logging retention policy, SSO coverage matrix, change control evidence, incident response runbook).

Sam: I'll post a sprint-by-sprint execution plan and contractor budget estimate by Monday. Call out blockers: SSO provider onboarding, log retention pipeline, and infra snapshot readiness.

Chris: I'll prep the infra freeze calendar and a short production change playbook.

deploy-bot: nightly-deploy 1719460500 — paused for targeted canary runs during proposed audit window per request.

Maya: Great. Owners aligned. We'll reconvene Tuesday 10am to lock scope and OK the contract language. Thanks all.
